newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso holds strength as investors eye stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso holds strength as investors eye stocks.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained its early strength late Wednesday morning, with foreign investors selling dollars to invest in stocks as the bourse marched into record territory, dealers said.
"The market is flooded with dollars. Foreign investors are weighing in," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were trading 1.7 and 1.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7640/7.7680 and 7.7610/7.7650 per dollar.
The 48-hour contract had earlier firmed to 7.7590/7.7610 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso could nonetheless resume its recent advance due to heavy capital flows into Mexican financial markets.
The Mexican bourse leaped 140.30 points to a record 4,937.79 in late trade on foreign buyers.
Foreign investors also turned to Mexico due to the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which had gained 27/32 to yield 6.33 percent in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 5.5 centavos firmer at 7.7520/7.7550 per dollar.
